overview.title: Live synthetic shirt
overview.brief: A white woven button-up shirt with long sleeves, practical tails and tasteful frills. Choose coherent editable construction details.

design.rationale: AI suggestions: use a relaxed woven block with straight-cap long sleeves and button cuffs with bound underarm openings. Sleeve length starts at the dropped shoulder and includes cuff depth; sleeve and cuff dimensions are design assumptions, not body measurements. Interpret practical tails as a curved hem with a longer back, not split coat tails. Narrow front-opening frills with modest gathering provide restrained decoration. A straight collar stand and plain rectangular collar fall complete the button-up design; this is not a shaped tailored collar. Retain the entered flare of 1. All dimensions, proportions and sewing allowances require owner review.

construction.note: AI-suggested sequence: confirm sizing inputs, length convention, shoulder drop, sleeve reach and cuff/collar clearance before cutting. Test fabric shrinkage, opacity and interfacing compatibility.

construction.operation: Prepare front frills and button plackets
construction.note: AI suggestion: narrowly finish exposed frill edges, gather to the proposed fullness and capture attachment edges at the front plackets. Confirm frill endpoints and keep buttonholes accessible.

AI suggestion: assemble the plain rectangular collar fall and straight stand, then attach to the neckline. Review the resulting collar shape in a sample; seam finish and interfacing placement remain to be confirmed.
AI suggestion: bind underarm sleeve openings, attach straight-cap sleeves to the dropped shoulders, then close sleeve and side seams. Confirm seam finishing on a fabric sample.
AI suggestion: assemble interfaced cuffs and attach at sleeve ends. Review sleeve-to-cuff fullness distribution, overlap and closed clearance before final stitching.

AI suggestion: use a narrow turned hem suited to the curved longer back edge. Confirm turn depth and transition smoothness in a sample; the proposed 10 mm seam allowance is not a resolved hem specification.

AI suggestion: sample buttonholes, finalize button positions and attach buttons. Measure the proposed POMs and review movement, collar comfort, frill behavior and tail coverage before approving further work.

warnings: Digital construction draft, not a physically fitted or sewing-validated pattern. Make a toile and check wearing ease, neck/head passage, cuff passage, collar roll and mobility before cutting final fabric.

All drafting dimensions are reviewed design assumptions. Neck width and armhole depth use disclosed synthetic proportions: bust/12 and bust/10 + 110 mm. Torso quarter width = (max(bust, hip) + ease)/4. No anatomical arm, wrist or neck measurements are inferred.

Each named left/right torso and sleeve is cut once as a mirrored pair. Plackets, cuffs and collar templates are cut twice for shell/facing; same-template interfacing is listed separately in derived materials. No fold-cut torso edges.

Uniform 10 mm outward cut-line offset includes seam and single-turn overlocked edge finishing. Offsets use sampled curves, miter limit 3, and polygon validity/containment checks. Double-turn hems, grading, fabric shrinkage, turn-of-cloth and physical print calibration are not validated.

The brief, references, construction text and requirement statuses are preserved but not interpreted by the geometry worker. Only validated structured garment controls and body values drive geometry; textual coverage remains subject to review.
